what_matters.head: US stocks had their biggest rally in about seven months on Monday: the S&P 500 fund rose 2.4% and the chip fund 7.5%.
what_matters.detail: Yahoo Finance said tech and industrial stocks led a comeback from last week's sell-off, helped by falling energy prices. US crude fell 5.5%. Reuters said oil fell after Trump said on Monday he plans to hold off from new strikes on Iran, following appeals from countries in the region. The chip fund is still down 3.0% over five sessions. The seven-month comparison is Investing.com's.

what_matters.head: Nvidia fell 4.3% on a day the chip fund rose 7.5%, on more than 2.6 times its average volume.
what_matters.detail: Its board is investigating whether chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, after he admitted an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. On Monday Trump said the FBI is looking into it and that he thinks Huang will "be in good shape". Shareholders filed a proposed class action against Huang and the company the same day. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called for limits on chip sales to China in the annual defence bill. Nvidia said its board has confidence in Huang. China's foreign ministry called the spying claim groundless. All from Reuters. Nvidia's results are due on 17 Nov.

what_matters.head: US October CPI is out at 21:30 SGT tonight, and CoreWeave reports about 05:05 SGT Wednesday.
what_matters.detail: Forecasts are for prices to rise 0.3% on the month and 0.2% excluding food and energy, after 0.6% and 0.3% in September (Yahoo Finance). It is the last CPI report before the Fed's 9 Dec decision. CoreWeave's own forecast for Q3 revenue is $3.4–3.6B, and analysts expect about $3.5B.

after_data.text: TSMC's October revenue was NT$586.9B, up 59.7% from a year earlier and about 14.7% above September (computed from TSMC's monthly figures). That is about 34–35% of the range its Q4 forecast implies, in the first of three months (computed at the forecast's own exchange rate). It came out on Tuesday afternoon and is not in Monday's US prices.
Infineon reported at 14:30 SGT; the figures are under Earnings. Its shares rose more than 6% in Frankfurt on Tuesday (Investing.com). That comes after Monday's rise, which is the one in the data.

South Korea's KOSPI was up 4.3% and Singapore's STI 1.6% around midday. Taiwan's index rose as much as 6.4% after regulators cut short-selling limits (Investing.com). The Seoul and Singapore prices in the data are from the same morning.
At 17:30 SGT Brent was down a further 2.6% at $90.18 and US crude 2.4% at $84.74. Brent had settled 5.85% lower on Monday (Reuters). Tuesday's fall is not in Monday's US prices.

out.text: Reported at 14:30 SGT Tuesday, after the data run. Fiscal Q4 (July–September): revenue €4.706B and segment profit €1.119B, a 23.8% margin. Revenue matched what analysts expected and segment profit was slightly above (Investing.com). Fiscal 2026 revenue was €16.353B, up 12%. The company's forecast for fiscal 2027 is revenue of about €20B, growth of more than 20%, and free cash flow of about €1.8B after €3.0–3.5B of investment. Investing.com said the revenue forecast was slightly above what analysts expected and the free cash flow forecast below. Infineon expects its data-centre power revenue, AI and classical together, to grow from €2.2B to close to €4B. That is not like-for-like with its earlier AI-only target of about €2.5B. Its forecast for the current quarter is revenue of about €4.6B. Proposed dividend: €0.38 a share, up €0.03.

recent.headline: US stocks had their biggest rally in about seven months on Monday: the S&P 500 fund rose 2.4% and the chip fund 7.5%.
Chip stocks bounced on Friday after their worst sell-off since 2020: the chip fund rose 3.5% and AMD 11%.
Wall Street's AI stocks sold off hard: the S&P 500 fund fell 4.4%, about 6.6 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund 12.2%.
Wall Street rose after the Democratic sweep, led by Microsoft and Amazon, while chip and data-centre stocks fell.
The AP projects that Democrats win both the House and the Senate, and US stock futures and Asian chip stocks fell on it.
